output:
Northbridge Library might keep its doors open later for a six-week trial starting October 5. If this happens, the library will stay open until 9 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays, rather than closing at 6 pm. The library has set aside $4,800 to pay for the extra staff needed during this period.

The goal is to make it easier for people to visit if they cannot get there during standard work hours. This trial does not include opening on Sundays, and the library hasn't decided if these later hours will continue once the six weeks are over. All current daytime services will stay the same.

Staff will count how many people visit during these extra hours and ask users to fill out a feedback form if they want to. The library will use this data to see if people want the service, though they acknowledge that people who do not visit the library won't be represented in the responses. Once the trial ends, the library committee will look at the attendance figures, what the staffing cost, and the feedback to decide if they should suggest a permanent change. Because of this, starting the trial does not mean the longer hours are guaranteed to stay.

source:
The Northbridge Library is considering an extension of its evening opening hours as part of a six-week pilot beginning on October 5. Under the proposal, the building would remain open until 9 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays instead of closing at 6 pm. The library has allocated $4,800 to cover additional staffing during the trial.

The proposed change is intended to improve access for residents who cannot visit during normal working hours. However, the pilot would not include Sunday opening, and no decision has been made about continuing the extended schedule after the trial. Existing daytime services would remain available throughout the six weeks.

Staff would record visitor numbers during the additional hours and invite users to complete an optional feedback form. These measures would help the library assess demand, although the responses might not represent residents who do not attend. At the end of the pilot, the library committee would review attendance, staffing costs, and feedback before deciding whether to recommend a permanent change. Approval of the pilot would therefore not guarantee a lasting extension of opening hours.
